SMTO-SKL-0181 — SMTO isn't sure if your GitHub change went through

GUID: 3515af8d-e37c-5c7b-96ff-82c46fce23c9
Slug: github-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO sent a change to GitHub, such as a new issue, comment, review or update, but didn't get a clear answer back. GitHub may already have made the change, so asking again could create a duplicate.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On github.com, open the issue, pull request, run or release you were changing, and look for your new comment, review, issue or edit. GitHub may have made the change even though SMTO didn't get the confirmation.
  2. If the change is there, don't ask the Agent to do it again. Tell the Agent it is done. Repeating it could post a second comment, open a duplicate issue, or apply the change twice.
  3. Only if the change is clearly missing, ask the Agent to make it once more. SMTO deliberately won't repeat it on its own, because it can't tell a duplicate from the original.

What success looks like

  • The change appears exactly once on github.com.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your GitHub access in SMTO. If you find a duplicate, remove it on GitHub yourself rather than asking SMTO to guess which one to keep.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GitHub write lost a reliable result (connection failure, timeout, 5xx/408/redirect status, malformed or oversized reply, cancellation after dispatch, or no returned object id), so the change may have been applied.

What this means

  • A GitHub write encounters transport failure, server/timeout/redirect status, malformed or oversized acknowledgement, or missing required returned object identity. The write may have applied despite its missing or invalid acknowledgement. Read exact provider state and reconcile it before another mutation; matching text alone does not prove attribution.

Why this can happen

  • A GitHub write encounters transport failure, server/timeout/redirect status, malformed or oversized acknowledgement, or missing required returned object identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact object IDs and retained provider evidence for the original mutation.

How to fix it

  • Do not replay the request. Read the exact object (issue, pull request, run, release or asset) by its GitHub number or ID and compare its current state with the intended change. New issues, pull requests, comments and reviews cannot be safely deduplicated by matching text; decide on any further write only after that read.
  • Do not replay this mutation. Read the exact object and inspect provider identifiers/state. Comments, reviews and creates cannot be deduplicated safely by matching text.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not replay this mutation. Read the exact object and inspect provider identifiers/state. Comments, reviews and creates cannot be deduplicated safely by matching text.

How to verify the fix

  • Remote state is reconciled before any new write; matching comments or review text do not establish deduplication.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The write may have applied despite its missing or invalid acknowledgement. Read exact provider state and reconcile it before another mutation; matching text alone does not prove attribution.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
